heroSub: Five boutique-style stays in Chanthaburi we've reviewed in depth — a minimalist blue-toned hotel with a pool in town, a city hotel with a full pool-and-sauna setup, a fresh boutique with spotless rooms near the mall, a quiet art gallery set in a garden, and a small owner-run hotel. From about ฿700–1,200/night.
introH2: 🏙️ What kinds of boutique stays does Chanthaburi have, and how do you pick the right one?
introHtml: First, let's be straight: Chanthaburi has no ski resorts — it's an eastern coastal town known for fruit, gems and good food. But "stylish boutique stays" in Chanthaburi come in more shapes than you'd expect, and that's what makes choosing here fun. Some are minimalist blue-and-white hotels that feel new and have a swimming pool right in town. Some are city hotels that pack in a big pool and a sauna for just over a thousand baht. Some are boutiques that only opened in 2023, with brand-new spotless rooms near the mall and market. Some are art galleries in a quiet garden away from the bustle. And some are small hotels where the owner looks after guests like they're welcoming you home. A lot of people pick the wrong style for their trip — say, wanting to explore the old town on foot but ending up on the outskirts where you need a car, and feeling stranded. This article rounds up 5 boutique stays in Chanthaburi we've reviewed in depth — across the town centre, the Tha Chang area and the outskirts — all drawn from reading real guest reviews, telling you the upsides and the honest caveats, comparing prices across 3 sites, with direct booking links for each.
mrtHtml: Chanthaburi has no commercial airport and no metro. Most people drive from Bangkok in about 3.5–4 hours, or take a van/coach into town. The nearest airports are Trat (TDX) or U-Tapao (UTP), then onward by car. The areas covered here: town centre, Rak Sakchamun / Phraya Trang Road — easy in and out of the old town, the Chanthaboon riverside community, the mall and the market, ideal if you want to eat, shop and sightsee in town. Tha Chang — a quieter side with a garden feel, about a 10 min drive into town. Tha Chang outskirts — peaceful, good for resting and as a base before heading to the beaches at Chao Lao–Khung Wiman or onward to Koh Chang. Almost every Chanthaburi stay has free parking, since most guests drive themselves.

entries.name: Blue Rabbit Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Town centre·Rak Sakchamun Rd · near Wat Khao Kaeo
entries.addr: 188 Moo 2, Rak Sakchamun Rd, Tha Chang, Mueang Chanthaburi
entries.storyHtml: If there's one Chanthaburi stay with a review score high enough to catch your eye, plenty of voices point here — Blue Rabbit Hotel is a 79-room minimalist blue-and-white hotel in central Chanthaburi, on Rak Sakchamun Rd in Tha Chang, with the highest real-review score in this article at 9.4 from 112 reviews on Trip.com. It opened around 2016 and has had some upgrades since. What makes people fall for it is the feeling of a small design hotel that looks new and immaculately clean — open the door and you're met with an easy blue-and-white palette throughout, living up to its name, the "blue rabbit." The thing reviews mention first is the cleanliness, praised almost unanimously; many say it's spotless in every corner and the rooms smell fresh, never musty. What sets it apart from similarly priced hotels in town is the outdoor pool with a kids' pool and free fitness room — hard to find at this price in central Chanthaburi. The 56 sqm family room, which fits up to 4 single beds, is a favourite for families and groups of friends because the per-head cost works out cheap. Add wide free parking, which matters a lot for anyone driving to Chanthaburi. The honest caveats from reviews: rooms facing the street get some traffic noise, especially during the day; the pool is a small one for cooling off rather than serious swimming; breakfast can be limited in quantity or variety at times; and although it's in town, you still need a car to reach the market and restaurant areas — not everything is within walking distance. In short, if you're driving to Chanthaburi and want an in-town stay that's clean, has a pool, easy parking and a price that won't balloon, Blue Rabbit ticks almost every box — and that's why its review score holds as high as 9.4.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're a light sleeper, ask for an inner room or one facing the pool to avoid traffic noise out front. Groups often take the 56 sqm family room — better value than booking several separate rooms — and hit the pool in the morning before heading out to the old town.

entries.name: New Travel Lodge Hotel
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Town centre·Rak Sakchamun Rd · 5 min to Robinson
tags: 🏊 Big pool with plenty of lounging space
entries.addr: 14/5 Moo 3, Rak Sakchamun Rd, Tha Chang, Mueang Chanthaburi
entries.storyHtml: Among Chanthaburi stays, if you measure by sheer number of reviews, New Travel Lodge Hotel has the most in this article — around 667 — a name locals have known for years. It's a mid-size 3-star hotel (roughly 100–140 rooms) on Rak Sakchamun Rd in Tha Chang, sitting right in town, only about a 5 min drive from Robinson Chanthaburi, so finding food, shopping or catching an evening movie is easy. What makes people pick it is that it packs big-hotel facilities in for just over a thousand baht. The number-one draw is a large outdoor pool that many reviews agree is roomy with plenty of lounging space around it — families with kids can splash about comfortably. Then there's the sauna and cold plunge, singled out for praise as a good setup, ideal for alternating hot and cold after a full day out, plus a fitness room, steam room, massage room and karaoke. Review scores sit in the 8.4–9.0 range depending on the platform — Trip.com shows around 9.0, while Booking sits around 8.4 from a larger review base. The honest part: this is a long-established hotel with some rooms renovated, so room quality "depends on which zone you get" — reviewers in newly renovated rooms praise them as clean and comfortable, while some older-building rooms look dated with fairly firm beds. The tip from reviews is to specifically request a renovated room when booking, since the price usually isn't much different. Other notes from reviews: some facilities show their age and aren't brand-new; the hotel takes both leisure guests and events/seminars, so weekends can get some event noise. In short, if you weigh "a big pool and full sauna on a budget + a central location" over a brand-new room, this is hard to beat at the same price in town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Request a renovated room when you book, since quality varies a fair bit but prices are close. Check the opening hours for the pool, sauna and cold plunge in advance, and use it as a base for the town and the Chao Lao beaches.

entries.name: Trimm Chanthaburi
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Town centre·Phraya Trang Rd · near mall/market
entries.addr: 89 Phraya Trang Rd, Wat Mai, Mueang Chanthaburi
entries.storyHtml: If the older hotels in Chanthaburi sell familiarity, Trimm Chanthaburi sells something harder to find — newness. It's a small boutique hotel of just 37 rooms that only opened in 2023, on Phraya Trang Rd in Wat Mai, central Chanthaburi, near the department store, market and hospital. What sets it apart from the town's older stays is that everything is still in good shape — furniture, walls and bathrooms still feel new. The phrase real reviews repeat most is "big rooms, cold AC, very clean bathroom" — cleanliness especially scores as high as 9.4, higher than any other category. Many say the rooms are larger than expected for the price and quiet at night. Most rooms are Superior Twin with 2 single beds, or Superior King at around 25 sqm, decorated in a warm contemporary style with a private balcony in every room. There's a restaurant and lounge bar serving Thai, Chinese and European food, a café, and a rooftop area to catch the evening breeze, plus free parking. The result is a real-review score reaching 9.1 from 172 reviews on Trip.com — surprisingly high for a stay starting at only around ฿850. The honest caveats to know: the hotel has no lift, so upper-floor rooms mean carrying bags up the stairs — a hassle for anyone with lots of luggage or older travellers. There's no pool or large fitness room. In the rainy season some rooms can feel damp or musty, and you may run into a bit of dust or ants, as with small hotels. And on platforms with more international reviewers like TripAdvisor, the score runs lower than on the Thai side, with some reviews unimpressed by service at times. In short, if you want a new, clean room in town on a light budget and just need a base to head out and eat, shop and sightsee, Trimm is genuinely better than its price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The hotel has no lift, so if you have lots of luggage or are travelling with older family, ask for a ground-floor room when booking. Check whether your rate includes breakfast, since some starting rates don't, and use the central location to plan eating, gem shopping and a riverside visit in one day.

rooms.type: Dara Green View King (full garden view)

tags: 🌳 Quiet garden, balcony in every room
entries.addr: 69/5 Moo 5, Soi Rak Sakchamun 24, Tha Chang, Mueang Chanthaburi
entries.storyHtml: If the other stays in this article sell in-town convenience, Pimdara Hotel sells the opposite — quiet and good taste. It's a small 36-room hotel built around an "art gallery" concept in the Tha Chang area of Mueang Chanthaburi, set just a little out from the bustle of the town centre. What sets it apart from similarly priced stays is that the common areas and corridors are decorated with paintings and artwork telling the stories and landmarks of Chanthaburi, so it feels like walking through a little gallery rather than an ordinary hotel. Wake up, open the balcony door and you find a green garden and quiet air with no traffic noise — because every room has a private balcony facing the garden. Real reviews agree the rooms are clean, larger than the price suggests, with attractive bathrooms and good water pressure, and the balcony is the part many love most. There's an outdoor pool set among the garden (open roughly 7:00–19:00), a fitness room, karaoke, free parking and an airport shuttle. The score is 8.9 from 158 reviews on Trip.com, and TripAdvisor ranks it #10 of 28 hotels in Chanthaburi. Several international reviews even say it's surprisingly cheaper than comparable resorts in the area. The honest trade-offs from reviews: the location is outside the commercial district, so you need a car — without one, getting around is tough, since hailing a ride in Chanthaburi isn't as easy as in a big city. Soundproofing between rooms isn't great, so you may hear the room next door. Some rooms have fairly firm beds, in-room amenities are basic, and the hotel's food options are limited, so it's best to drive into town for dinner. In short, if you're driving yourself and value atmosphere, quiet and design over walking to everything, Pimdara is a stay whose value really stands out on atmosphere.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: This place suits people with a car best. If you want a full garden view, ask specifically for a Green View room, and if you're a light sleeper, ask for a room not adjoining others since soundproofing isn't great. Plan dinner in town or at the Chanthaboon riverside community ahead of time.

entries.name: Baanlugchange Hotel
entries.badge: 💛 Attentive owner · cheapest in the group
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Tha Chang outskirts · ~10 min into town
tags: 💛 Owner looks after you like home
entries.addr: 25/89 Moo 5, Soi Rak Sakchamun 16, Tha Chang, Mueang Chanthaburi
entries.storyHtml: We close the article with the stay that has the most heart in the group — Baanlugchange Hotel. It's a small hotel of about 22 rooms at the 2-star level, run and looked after closely by the owner, set in a quiet lane in the Tha Chang area on the outskirts of Chanthaburi, about a 10 min drive from the town and the Chanthaboon riverside community. This isn't a beachfront resort or a city chain hotel, but a small stay that sells well-kept simplicity — several international reviews use the phrase "simple but smart clean rooms," meaning the rooms aren't fancy but they're clean and cleverly laid out. What real reviews agree on, and what pushes the overall score as high as 8.9, is the quiet, the cleanliness, and an owner who looks after guests with real care. Reviews consistently call the owner "very helpful" — helping call a ride into town, giving directions and recommending local eateries — and many feel more like they're being welcomed at a friend's home than checking into an ordinary hotel. There's free parking, free Wi-Fi, a 24-hour front desk, laundry service, and a coffee/drinks corner reviews praise; some rooms have a balcony or a sitting area with town or hill views. Prices start at only around ฿700/night, the cheapest in this article. The honest caveats to know before booking: there's no breakfast and no hotel restaurant, so you have to eat out (but a 10 min drive into town gets you to Nam Phu market with Chanthaburi noodles, mu chamuang and plenty of local food). It's on the outskirts, about 10 min from the tourist area, so you need a car or to call a ride into town. There's no pool and no fitness room, and the rooms are simple, in line with the 2-star level. In short, if you're driving to Chanthaburi yourself and want a clean, quiet, budget room with an owner who looks after you like family — or a stopover before heading on to Koh Chang–Trat — Baanlugchange is a deal that's hard to find at this price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Driving yourself is the best value here thanks to free parking and the outskirts location. If you have no vehicle, ask the owner about arranging a ride in advance. There's no breakfast, so start the morning at the hotel's coffee corner then drive into town for Chanthaburi food at Nam Phu market. If you want a hill-view balcony, request it when booking.

faqTitle: FAQ — common questions travellers ask about Chanthaburi boutique stays

faq.q: ❓ Which is the best boutique stay in Chanthaburi?
faq.a: It depends on your trip style. If you go by review score and want a pool in town, Blue Rabbit Hotel at 9.4 is the highest in the article, minimalist blue tones with a pool and fitness. If you go by number of reviews and full facilities, New Travel Lodge has the most reviews at around 667, with a big pool and sauna. If you want a new, clean room, Trimm just opened in 2023. If you want a quiet, design-led atmosphere, Pimdara is an art gallery in a garden. And if you want a small stay with an attentive owner on the lightest budget, Baanlugchange.

No. Chanthaburi is an eastern coastal town of Thailand, known for fruit, gems, food and the Chanthaboon riverside community — not a snow town or a high mountain for skiing. This article rounds up the town's "stylish boutique stays," from minimalist design hotels and new boutiques to art galleries and small owner-run hotels.

faq.q: ❓ How much do Chanthaburi boutique stays cost?
faq.a: In this article, prices start at about ฿700–1,200 per night. The most accessible are Baanlugchange from ฿700 and Trimm / Pimdara from ฿850. New Travel Lodge starts at ฿1,100 and Blue Rabbit at ฿1,200. All prices are approximate starting prices from standard rooms; during the fruit season and long weekends prices can run higher than usual, so compare 3 sites before booking.

faq.q: ❓ Which area should you stay in for a Chanthaburi trip?
faq.a: Town centre (Rak Sakchamun / Phraya Trang Rd) suits people who want to eat, shop and sightsee in town, with easy access to the old town, the riverside community, the mall and the market (Blue Rabbit, New Travel Lodge, Trimm). Tha Chang and the outskirts suit people who want quiet and a garden feel, using it as a base for resting then driving about 10 min into town (Pimdara, Baanlugchange) — but you need a car.

faq.q: ❓ Which Chanthaburi boutique stays have a pool?
faq.a: In this article, the ones with a pool are Blue Rabbit Hotel (outdoor pool + kids' pool, in town), New Travel Lodge (big pool + sauna + cold plunge) and Pimdara Hotel (outdoor pool in a garden). Trimm and Baanlugchange have no pool because they're small stays, but they stand out for new, clean rooms and personal care instead.

faq.q: ❓ Do you need a car in Chanthaburi · how far ahead should you book?
faq.a: Chanthaburi has no commercial airport and no metro, so most people drive from Bangkok in about 3.5–4 hours, and almost every stay has free parking. If you stay in Tha Chang or the outskirts (Pimdara, Baanlugchange) you should have a car, since you can't walk to the sights. For booking, during the fruit season (Apr–Jun) and long weekends/New Year, book 1–2 months ahead; other times 2–3 weeks is enough. Every platform offers Free Cancellation, so it's worth locking in a rate like that if your plans aren't firm, then comparing Agoda / Booking / Trip.com for the best price.
